title: Duat: Ancient Egypt Sound Effects
shortText: 137 Ancient Egypt SFX: tomb traps, spells of the gods, scarabs and mummies, bronze weapons, 5 loops. WAV + OGG.
html:
Ancient Egypt, as one sound

137 Ancient Egypt sound effects in WAV and OGG for any game engine (Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and HTML5): tomb mechanisms, hieroglyph puzzle stones, 8 spells of the gods with a charge, a release and a fizzle each, scarabs, cobras and mummies, bronze weapons, a papyrus and stone interface, rewards, accents and 5 ambience loops. Royalty free for commercial games, no credit required. A free demo of 20 sounds is on this page.

Licence, up front

Royalty free. Commercial use. No attribution required. Use it in as many games as you like, on any platform. The one thing you may not do is resell or redistribute the sounds themselves as a sound pack. The plain language terms ship as LICENSE.txt, with a copy and paste credit line for anyone who wants one. Everything is synthesised from code, so there is no upstream sample licence behind it.

Hear it first

There is a free demo on this page: 20 sounds copied unaltered from the paid files. The sun disc spell in all three phases, the sarcophagus lid and the sand flood trap in every state, the scarab swarm at all five densities, five interface cues and the burial chamber.

One tomb, one palette

Every sound is built from the materials of an Egyptian tomb and temple: cut limestone and granite, cast bronze, beaten gold, glazed faience, fired clay, cedar, reed, linen, and the sand that runs under all of it. Every one shot sits in the same limestone chamber, so a game set on the Nile stops borrowing a generic dungeon.

The tomb, whole lifecycles

  • Sarcophagus lid: grind open, slide (loop), slam
  • Slab door: rise, fall, locked
  • Sand flood trap: release, pour (loop), drain
  • Pressure stone: press, release
  • Hidden passage: open, close
  • Canopic jar: open, break
  • Torch: ignite, burn (loop), snuff
  • Cobra: hiss, strike
  • Mummy: rise, shamble, unravel, collapse
  • Khopesh: draw, cut, clash
  • Sling: whirl (loop), release
  • Horn bow: draw, release

No two states of one mechanism, creature, weapon or material are the same sound renamed (33 pairs measured from the shipped files, 0 alike).

Eight spells, every phase

  • Sun disc: the sun god's disc gathering light and loosing it as one searing beam.
  • Death curse: a curse laid on the tomb robber: dust drawn in, a hollow low blow, breath leaving the room.
  • Sand vortex: a storm of sand summoned as a single spell, spun up, thrown and let fall.
  • Glyph bolt: a carved sign torn off the wall and thrown as a bolt of gold light.
  • Healing wings: the goddess's wings folding over the wounded: a soft linen rush and a warm ring.
  • Ankh revive: the ankh raised over the fallen, its gold ringing as breath returns.
  • Eye reveal: the eye of the falcon god opening to show what is hidden.
  • Scarab ward: a scarab amulet closing a shell of bronze around its wearer.

Each spell ships a charge, a release and a fizzle, so a magic system can wire the hold, the hit and the cancel. Checked from the shipped files, not promised: across the spell by phase grid the spell changes the sound and so does the phase (108 pairs, 0 alike). Wiring it is one string: sun_disc_charge, death_curse_release.

A swarm that thickens, a puzzle that lights up

  • The scarab swarm: five seamless loops from a few beetles crossing the sand to a flood of shells clattering over each other, each

rung brighter than the last. Wire the rung to how many beetles are near.

  • The glyph stones: a carved glyph lighting at five steps of a puzzle, for a sequence lock or a progress bar.

8 ladder steps measured from the shipped files, failing steps: 0.

The rest of the adventure

  • 11 puzzle sounds: glyph stones turning (three takes), the five lit stones, a sequence right, a sequence wrong and a chamber unsealed.
  • 12 handled materials: bronze, alabaster, gold, faience, linen and reed, each picked up and put down.
  • 8 rewards: coins (two takes), a gem, an ankh, a scarab charm, a relic found, a treasure revealed and a papyrus found.
  • 15 interface sounds: scrolls unrolling and rolling, a limestone tablet opening and closing, select, confirm, cancel, page turn, inventory, error, quest update, save and cursor takes.
  • 6 encounter and turn cues and 6 accents: a struck bronze gong, a sistrum shaken (two takes) and three reveal accents, every one a single struck or shaken gesture, never a melody.
  • 5 ambience loops: a burial chamber, a hall of columns in the wind, a temple court at noon, the Nile reeds at dusk and a desert camp at night (no storm).

Fit

  • WAV and OGG for every file, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz, mono, with a naming manifest listing every file by group.
  • 15 seamless loops with loop points in both formats, and none on a one shot.
  • 11 variation sets whose takes differ in length and in brightness.
  • One loudness band: the inner 80 percent of the pack sits inside 1.09 dB, so a falling slab and a papyrus cursor share a mix.
  • Import notes for Unity, Unreal, Godot, GameMaker, RPG Maker and the web, and pack_proof.json with a sha256 and a measurement for every file: 1259 checks, 0 failed.

Already own our other sound packs?

Every file here was measured against every file in the studio's 5 nearest packs (dungeon mechanisms and traps, the wuxia era suite, place beds, medieval impacts and weather: 83022 pairs, on spectral shape and on envelope, each tolerant of a transposition): 83022 of 83022 are separate sounds. The proof ships in the download as cross_pack_proof.json.

Honest limits

These are synthesised sounds designed for games, not field recordings from a real tomb: cut stone, bronze, gold, faience, clay, cedar, reed, linen and sand. The figures above are signal measurements, not a claim that anything sounds good; that is what the free demo is for. There are no voices and no music: the creatures are foley (a cobra's hiss is air, a mummy is linen and dust), and the accents are single struck or shaken sounds.

AI disclosure, stated truthfully: the code that generates these sounds was written with AI assistance. The sounds themselves are self contained procedural synthesis by Core Systems Asset Factory, with no generative audio model at any point. The cover is an AI generated illustration, and the store plates are drawn by AI written code from the pack's own waveforms.

More from the same studio

  • Verdant 51, Pyramid Tombs, a tileset of Egyptian hieroglyph halls, a burial chamber and sand traps, for the tomb these sounds belong in.
  • Desert, a music pack of caravans, dunes and a sunken city.
  • Portcullis, dungeon doors, chests, levers and traps, for the dungeons beyond the tomb.
  • Sixfold, elemental spell casting chains, for a wider spellbook.
  • Jianghu, the same idea for the world of wuxia: one era, one palette.
